title: Lightning on Set
summary: Rig a giant plate capacitor on a film set: charge it, set the gap, slide in panels and fire a flash on cue to wake a robot.
subject: physics
concepts: A dielectric multiplies C by K
Dielectric strength of air, about 3 × 10⁶ V/m
Energy density of the field, u = ½ε₀E²
learningOutcome: The student can use Q = CV and C = Kε₀A/d, say how a dielectric changes Q and V with the charger on or off, and use air’s breakdown field and u = ½ε₀E² to size a flash.

levels.title: Wake-up charge
levels.adds: Baseline: the plates hold Q = CV, so set V = Q/C; at 3 kV or more per millimetre of air the gap breaks down and the rig flashes over (Section 2.11).
hints: Q = CV: nanofarads times kilovolts gives microcoulombs.
So V = Q/C. Remember 1000 pF = 1 nF.
Keep V below 3 kV for every millimetre of air between the plates.

levels.title: Set the gap
levels.adds: New idea: C = ε₀A/d, so a smaller gap gives a bigger C, and a panel of constant K filling the gap multiplies C by K (Ex 2.5, 2.8).
hints: Find the C you need from C = Q/V first.
C = ε₀A/d with A in m² and d in metres; ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m.
Halving the gap doubles C; a panel of constant K multiplies it by K.

levels.title: Slide in a panel
levels.adds: New idea: with the charger connected V stays fixed and Q grows K times; unplugged, Q stays fixed and V falls K times (Ex 2.9).
hints: The panel multiplies C by K either way.
Connected: the charger holds V, so Q = KCV.
Unplugged: Q cannot change, so V = Q/(KC).

levels.title: Flash on cue
levels.adds: New idea: the energy lives in the field, u = ½ε₀E² per cubic metre; when air breaks down the flash releases u × A × d (Section 2.15).
hints: Air breaks down at E = 3 × 10⁶ V/m, so a gap d fires at V = E·d.
u = ½ε₀E² is the energy in each cubic metre of field.
The flash carries U = u × A × d. Solve for the plate area A.

misconceptions: The capacitance depends on the charge on the plates
Halving the gap halves the capacitance
A dielectric changes the charge whether or not the battery is connected
The potential difference rises when a dielectric is inserted
The energy of a capacitor sits on its plates, not in the field between them
